report_name: Wall Street Giants Targeted in Coordinated AI Vishing Campaign

threat_actors.name: UNC6671
threat_actors.description: A financially motivated threat actor targeting major financial firms using an AI-powered voice-phishing (vishing) campaign to steal Microsoft 365 and Okta credentials via adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing sites.
threat_actors.goals: To steal credentials (username, password) and intercept multi-factor authentication (MFA) tokens or session cookies in real-time, thereby gaining full access to victim accounts for data exfiltration.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Voice
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor UNC6671 conducted a voice-phishing (vishing) campaign, calling employees on their personal mobile phones to manipulate them.

attack_patterns.name: Generate Deepfakes
attack_patterns.description: The attackers used AI-powered voice cloning technology to mimic the voices of corporate IT helpdesk personnel, creating a sense of legitimacy and urgency to make the social engineering more convincing.

attack_patterns.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
attack_patterns.description: Victims were directed to adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing sites that acted as a reverse proxy to capture passwords and real-time MFA tokens by forwarding credentials to the real service and relaying the MFA prompt back to the victim.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
attack_patterns.description: The ultimate goal of the AitM phishing attack was to steal the authenticated session cookie after the victim entered their credentials and MFA token, allowing the attacker to take over the session.

attack_patterns.name: Email Collection
attack_patterns.description: After gaining access to an account, the threat actor used automated tools to exfiltrate sensitive data from the user's email account.

attack_patterns.name: Impersonation
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor impersonated corporate IT helpdesk personnel during the vishing calls, using AI voice cloning to enhance the deception.

infrastructure.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle Phishing Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Highly convincing, lookalike login portals for Microsoft 365 and Okta that function as reverse proxies to capture credentials and MFA tokens in real-time.

indicators.name: Suspicious Login from Unfamiliar Location
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Login from Unfamiliar Location
id: 2f8b1c3a-9e4d-4f8a-b1c3-a9e8d7c6b5a4
status: experimental
description: Detects successful logins to Okta or Entra ID from unfamiliar IP addresses, ASNs, or geolocations, which could indicate a compromised account following a vishing attack.
references:
  - https://thenextweb.com/news/vishing-campaign-blackstone-kkr-cme-finance-firms
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-08
tags:
  - attack.t1078.004
  - attack.initial_access
level: medium
logsource:
  product: okta
detection:
  selection:
    outcome.result: 'SUCCESS'
    security_context.is_proxy: false
  filter_known_location:
    client.geographical_context.country: 'United States' # Example known-good country
  condition: selection and not filter_known_location
indicators.description: Detects successful logins from unfamiliar IP addresses, ASNs, or geolocations, especially if they occur shortly after a known vishing attempt. This can indicate a compromised account.

indicators.name: Suspicious MFA Device Enrollment
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious MFA Device Enrollment
id: 8d7c6b5a-4f8a-4e9d-b1c3-a9e8d7c6b5a4
status: experimental
description: Detects the registration of a new MFA device, which attackers may attempt after compromising an account to establish persistence.
references:
  - https://thenextweb.com/news/vishing-campaign-blackstone-kkr-cme-finance-firms
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-08
tags:
  - attack.t1098
  - attack.persistence
level: high
logsource:
  product: okta
detection:
  selection:
    eventtype: 'user.mfa.factor.activate'
    outcome.result: 'SUCCESS'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects when a new MFA device is enrolled for a user account, which could be an attacker attempting to establish persistence after a credential compromise.
